title: Apply health and safety to a work area

lessons.title: Spotting hazards in your work area
lessons.html:
Hazard and risk

A hazard is anything that can hurt you or damage property. A risk is how likely it is to happen and how bad it would be. A loose cow in the kraal is a hazard. Walking in front of her in a narrow passage makes the risk high.

Types of hazards on a farm

TypeExamples
MachinesTractor PTO shafts, augers, chainsaws, belts and pulleys
ChemicalsSprays, dips, fuel, cleaning products
AnimalsKicks, horns, bites, bulls, snakes, bees
ElectricalDamaged cables, wet plugs, overloaded sockets
PhysicalSlippery floors, holes, heavy lifting, noise, heat and sun
FireDry veld, fuel stores, welding near hay

Look before you work

Every day, walk through your work area and ask: what could hurt someone here?

  • Are guards in place on machines?
  • Are walkways clear of tools, hoses and spills?
  • Are chemicals stored and labelled correctly?
  • Is there enough light?
  • Is the fire extinguisher in its place and not blocked?
  • Is everyone wearing the right protective clothing?

What to do with a hazard

  1. If it is safe and simple, fix it yourself, for example pick up a hose lying across the walkway.
  2. If you cannot fix it, warn others (put up a sign or barrier).
  3. Report it to your supervisor or health and safety representative straight away.

Under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 your employer must provide a safe workplace, and you must work safely and report unsafe conditions. You have a part to play.

A farm example

In the feed store, a worker sees that the grain auger guard is missing. He does not use the auger, puts a warning sign on the switch and tells his supervisor straight away. The guard is fixed before anyone gets hurt. That is how hazard spotting works.

lessons.title: Emergencies, illness and injury
lessons.html:
Know before it happens

In an emergency there is no time to learn. Know these things now:

  • Where the fire extinguishers, first aid box and emergency exits are.
  • Who the first aider is.
  • The emergency numbers on the notice board.
  • Where the assembly point is.
  • How to switch off the electricity and the machines in your area.

When an emergency happens

  1. Raise the alarm: shout, ring the bell or blow the whistle, and tell your supervisor.
  2. Make it safe: switch off machines and power if you can do it safely.
  3. Get people out: go to the assembly point and help others. Do not stop to collect belongings.
  4. Fight a small fire only if trained and safe: use the right extinguisher and keep your escape route behind you. Never fight a fire that is growing fast.
  5. Do not go back in until the person in charge says it is safe.

Limiting damage means stopping it from getting worse: closing a valve on a leaking tank, moving animals away from a veld fire, or putting sand on a fuel spill, but only when it is safe for you.

Illness or injury at work

  1. Check for danger to yourself before helping. Do not become a second casualty.
  2. Call the first aider and your supervisor.
  3. Do not move a badly injured person unless there is danger, such as fire.
  4. If you are trained, give basic first aid while you wait. Hands-on first aid training from an accredited provider is needed before you give first aid.
  5. Report every injury, even small cuts. It must be recorded, and you may be covered under COIDA.

Never

  • Never hide an injury or work on while hurt.
  • Never give someone medicine from your own bag.

Key points

  • A hazard can cause harm; risk is how likely and how serious.
  • Check your work area daily and report hazards.
  • Know where the extinguisher, first aid box and assembly point are.
  • In an emergency: raise the alarm, make safe, get out.
  • Report every injury and illness at work.

quiz.question: What is the first thing you should do when you discover a fire?
A hose lying across a walkway is easy to move safely. What should you do?

options.text: Move it and keep the walkway clear

quiz.question: When should you go back into a building after an evacuation?

options.text: When the person in charge says it is safe

quiz.question: Before you help an injured person, what must you check?

options.text: That there is no danger to yourself

quiz.question: You only need to report injuries that need a doctor.
